summary: kernel/templates/ is not listed in exclude_paths, so the full template tree (CLAUDE.md.template, bootloader-state.md.template, copilot-instructions.md.template, settings.json.template, platform-adapters/**) is copied verbatim into the extracted public product. D42 states '.azoth/kernel/ is created by install from kernel/' for consumers — but shipping the raw templates directory adds scaffold-internal tooling (bootloader templates, Cursor adapter templates, install.sh settings template) that is not meaningful for product consumers and may cause confusion about which files to edit.
evidence: sync-config.yaml exclude_paths: no entry for 'kernel/templates/' or 'kernel/templates/platform-adapters/'. ls kernel/templates/ shows: CLAUDE.md.template, bootloader-state.md.template, copilot-instructions.md.template, settings.json.template, platform-adapters/. Only README.public.azoth.md and ci-public-azoth.yml are intentional (emitted via emit_public_assets). D42 / D35 define kernel/ as governance docs for consumers; templates are scaffold tooling.
recommended_action: Add 'kernel/templates/' to product_extraction.exclude_paths in sync-config.yaml. The two intentional public templates (README.public.azoth.md, ci-public-azoth.yml) are already emitted by emit_public_assets — they do not need to survive into the extracted tree as raw templates. Also add a test in test_azoth_extract_product.py asserting that kernel/templates/ paths are absent from the output tree.

summary: The public README template hardcodes 'github.com/yiwei79' as the commercial-license contact. When this template is emitted by extract_product and shipped to consumers, every extracted azoth product tree will contain this personal GitHub link. If azoth is ever transferred, forked, or packaged by a different person/org, the emitted README will have stale/wrong maintainer identity that consumers see.
evidence: kernel/templates/README.public.azoth.md line: 'contact via [github.com/yiwei79](https://github.com/yiwei79)'. README_SUBSTITUTIONS dict in azoth_extract_product.py has only PRODUCT_NAME and DESCRIPTION — no MAINTAINER_URL or GITHUB_USER substitution key. DEFAULT_CLAUDE_SUBSTITUTIONS has GITHUB_USER but it is not used in README substitutions.
recommended_action: Add a README_SUBSTITUTIONS key (e.g., MAINTAINER_URL or CONTACT_URL) in both README.public.azoth.md (as {{MAINTAINER_URL}}) and in README_SUBSTITUTIONS in azoth_extract_product.py. Default value can remain 'github.com/yiwei79' so current behavior is unchanged, but the value is now overridable without editing the template. Also extend test_extract_minimal_tree to assert '{{' is absent from README.md in the output (similar to existing CLAUDE.md assertion).

summary: test_extract_minimal_tree does not set up or assert the LICENSE file in the extracted tree. The PolyForm Noncommercial license change is a critical P4-004 shipping requirement — consumers must receive a valid LICENSE. Since the test fixture doesn't create a LICENSE file and doesn't assert its presence, a regression that accidentally excludes or omits LICENSE from the extracted product would not be caught by this test.
evidence: test_extract_minimal_tree fixture creates: sync-config.yaml, kernel/templates/, skills/probe.md, .azoth/secret.yaml, tests/t.py, CLAUDE.md, azoth.yaml. No LICENSE file created. rels assertions only check .azoth/ and tests/ absence, skills/ and .github/ and README.md presence. No assertion for 'LICENSE' in rels.
recommended_action: Add a LICENSE stub to the test fixture (e.g., 'PolyForm Noncommercial...' as placeholder text) and assert 'LICENSE' in rels to confirm it copies through. This guards against a future exclude_paths entry accidentally excluding root LICENSE.
